title: Dynamic entitlement evaluation for streaming usage events
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Implement a low-latency entitlement evaluation layer for streaming usage events that powers console usage views and metrics pipelines. Current analytics endpoints perform coarse tenant-scoped filtering downstream which causes inconsistent visibility when events arrive out-of-order or when entitlements change. This ticket introduces a dynamic evaluation step at ingestion that evaluates per-event entitlements against the latest token/role state, supports incremental updates to entitlements, and emits visibility markers used by downstream aggregations and the Console UI.
background: We frequently see customer reports where usage dashboards show spikes or missing rows after entitlement changes or cross-tenant role delegations. Existing approaches either (a) re-run heavy joins for every query causing high cost, or (b) rely on late reprocessing windows that delay accurate dashboards. Streaming evaluation offers deterministic per-event visibility with bounded latency and allows downstream materialized views to be eventually consistent with minimal reprocessing.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming ingest annotates each usage event with a visibility_reason and normalized entitlement_token within 250ms p50 and 1s p95 under standard load
Rollout behind feature flag with canary to internal orgs; no errors >0.05% for CANARY orgs after 24h
Console usage views and per-route metrics reflect entitlement changes within 60s of a change for 95% of cases
Automated unit + integration tests covering role revocation, delegated access, and tenant-scoped masking
Observability: dashboards for eval latency, cache hit rate, eval errors, and rollback button exposed in Console
implementation_notes: Introduce Entitlement Eval Service (stateless HTTP/gRPC) colocated with the streaming ingest workers; evaluate policies using the same policy format as the Console RBAC service

Primary data source for entitlements: combination of snapshot cache (Redis) keyed by subject-token and changelog feed (CDC -> Kafka) for updates; prefer cache reads with async invalidation on CDC events
Support two evaluation modes: fast-path cache-only for reads where token TTL > 30s; strong-consistency mode that queries authoritative store (Authz DB) when TTL unknown or after write events
Emit annotated event attributes: visibility_flag (allowed|masked|denied), visibility_reason (explicit-role|delegation|default-tenant), token_version, eval_timestamp
Fall back to coarse-grained tenant filter only if Entitlement Eval service is unhealthy for >5s; feature flag controls fallbacks and strictness
Batch policy evals for high-throughput tenants using vectorized matcher to amortize policy parsing cost
Keep evaluation code independent of downstream schemas; produce only normalized attributes so materializers can consume without coupling
tradeoffs: Stateless eval service reduces complexity and scales horizontally but requires a highly available cache; alternative (stateful stream processor) would reduce cache reads but complicate upgrades
Cache-first approach improves latency but may serve slightly stale entitlements; we mitigate with CDC-driven invalidation and versioned tokens in event annotations
Strong-consistency mode increases p95 latency for edge cases; will be opt-in per-tenant during rollout
Vectorized batching increases throughput but requires careful backpressure handling between Kafka and eval workers
test_plan: Unit tests for policy matcher and attribute normalizer (100% branch coverage for new matcher)
Integration tests: deploy Entitlement Eval Service to staging, replay historical event window with simulated CDC order changes and validate final materialized view matches expected output
Load test: synthetic stream at 3x expected peak for top 10 tenants; assert p95 eval latency < 1s and cache hit rate > 80%
Chaos test: kill cache nodes and assert fallback path works and no data loss occurs
Security tests: ensure annotated event attributes do not leak PII and token_version values are irreversible
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary (redwood-infra org) for 48h; verify dashboards and rollout health metrics
Phase 2: Selected customers (3 customers across SMB/Enterprise) for 7 days; collect correctness and latency feedback
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% of production ingest traffic over 48h, then 100% after 7 days if SLOs met
Rollback criteria: >0.5% eval errors for 1h or >2x baseline alerting rates; automatic flag disable and backfill plan triggered
observability: Dashboards: 'Entitlement Eval - Latency', 'Entitlement Cache - HitRate', 'Eval Errors by Tenant', 'Visibility Drift (reconciler)'
Tracing: pass trace IDs through eval service and materializers; provide flamegraphs for hot policy paths
Alerts: p95 eval latency > 1.2s, error rate > 0.1% for 15m, cache miss rate > 40% sustained for 30m
Audit: log eval decisions (allow/deny/mask) to audit-log topic with sampling for privacy
security_considerations: Entitlement Eval must not persist raw tokens; store token_version and hashed subject identifiers only
Access controls: service-to-service mTLS and role-scoped RPC credentials for eval calls
Privacy: redact any user-identifying attributes from event annotations sent to materialization clusters
Security review required prior to phase 2 rollout
